trails.name: Southern Loop
trails.note: Marked with gray diamonds. About two-thirds is pasture or county/gravel road. Connects to Smith Creek Loop at Rutherford Bridge and to Moon Loop at the north end. The Forest Service names Paris Chapel as its trailhead; Dry Fork is described as the equestrian trailhead of the 36-mile trail; Rutherford Bridge is the stated junction with Smith Creek Loop.

trails.name: Smith Creek Loop
trails.note: Marked with orange diamonds. Between Boydsville and Rutherford Bridge. Crosses Smith Creek with no bridge. Grades of 10 to 12 percent; rated moderate.

trails.name: Moon Loop
trailheads: Moon Loop Trailhead (on Barnes Chapel Rd.)
trails.note: Marked with yellow diamonds. Two crossings of Big Branch Creek with no bridges. Stated as approximately 6.2 miles; a search summary reported about 7 miles on another Forest Service page.

trails.name: Pine Ridge Section
trails.note: Marked with gray diamonds; passes through Pine Ridge Recreation Area. Foot and mountain bike only, no horses; horse users are sent to Dry Fork, about 4 miles northeast on County Road 361.

notes: The Forest Service describes one 36-mile Cedar Creek Trail made of four sections: Southern Loop 22, Smith Creek Loop 5, Moon Loop 6.2, Pine Ridge Section 2.8 (sum 36.0). No Forest Service trail numbers were found. Open to hiking, mountain biking and horseback riding except the Pine Ridge Section (no horses). No motorized vehicles on the trail. Creek crossings on Smith Creek Loop (Smith Creek) and Moon Loop (Big Branch Creek, two) have no bridges. Much of the Southern Loop is pasture and county road. Dispersed camping allowed, no designated sites; potable water only at Dry Fork and Pine Ridge Recreation Areas. District contact given as Houston/Rolla/Cedar Creek Ranger District, 417-967-4194. The search summaries surfaced no Forest Service statement on private land crossings or hunting seasons, so none is recorded. A Forest Service trail map PDF exists (publication/Cedar%20Creek.pdf) but could not be read. Not read directly: www.fs.usda.gov is not reachable from this session; all facts are from search-result summaries of Forest Service pages, and the Barnes Chapel Rd. and Ginn Rd. trailhead directions in particular were garbled in those summaries.
